_about: karma's reads on players that the numbers can't see. Kept by hand. 'motor': high-intensity player whose output rises with his minutes; never take an under on him when a starter at his position is out. 'small_ball_5': plays centre in small lineups, so there is rebound upside when the bigs sit. 'primary_guard_defender': guards the opponent's main ball-handler, so his minutes hold up whatever happens to his shooting. 'rebounds_suppressed_with_giannis': fade this player's rebound overs when Giannis plays. 'low_mistake_trusted': the coach trusts him and his minutes are steady, but his output moves between stats, so prefer combo props. 'big_game_closer': plays more and is on the floor at the end of close or big games.

Baylor Scheierman.note: High-intensity player, maximises any minutes he gets (karma, 5 Nov 2026). Started for the resting Tatum on 4 Nov: 29 min, 9 pts, 11 reb; our under 12.5 PR lost. The model had him at 24.6 min and 4.5 reb.

Mario Hezonja.note: Big role for now (karma, 6 Nov). Peyton Watson has a nagging hamstring and could be in and out of the lineup all season. Hezonja is probably CLE's best defender on opposing primary guards, which keeps his minutes steady, and he plays the 5 when they go small, which is where the rebounds come from. Rebounding above his minutes: 31 Oct 20 min, 11 reb; 2 Nov 27 min, 12/8; 4 Nov 23 min, 12/8 after Allen left injured in Q1.
Mario Hezonja.review: 2026-12-01 (Watson coming back no longer ends the role on its own, given the nagging hamstring)

_team_notes.GSW: Source: Dunker Spot, 4 Nov. Forcing lots of turnovers; extra offensive rebounds from guards and wings; ice/shade sideline handoffs. Steph and Draymond sit some nights for maintenance. Niang +20 in 21 min vs PHX; Bassey a strong screener in random starts. Porzingis is out long-term (karma, 6 Nov): Draymond, Horford and Bassey cover centre. UPDATE 7 Nov AEDT: Porzingis announced he is stepping away from basketball to prioritise his health (Underdog / Bleacher Report; some outlets call it retirement). Treat him as gone for good: Draymond, Horford and Bassey are the centre rotation, Draymond in big games (karma).
_team_notes.DAL: Source: Dunker Spot, 4 Nov. Leads the league in zone possessions by a wide margin. Gafford leads them in offensive rebounds, with Risacher second. Max Christie's defence has been weak.
_team_notes.MIA: Source: Dunker Spot, 4 Nov. Luka torched them on the second night of a back-to-back: Davion Mitchell too small, Wiggins no answer, Bam only some good possessions. Elite guards can get loose against their perimeter defence.
_team_notes.OKC: karma, 7 Nov: with SGA and whoever else, OKC know how to win; they have won through constant lineup changes for two seasons. Measured (SGA's game logs): with SGA playing and one of Holmgren / J. Williams missing, 38-7 in 2024-25 and 40-5 in 2025-26; with both missing 5-0 and 5-1 (3-2 so far in 2026-27). So do not let our absence penalty sink OKC's team total/margin the way it would for a normal team; their system holds. Example (karma, verified in game logs): 9 Mar 2026 v DEN, OKC beat Jokic's Nuggets without J. Williams, Holmgren, Caruso AND Hartenstein; SGA 35/9/15 with 0 TO, tying Wilt's 126 straight 20-point games. Thunder Collective (6 Nov): Caruso back; new pieces Micah Peavy (POA defender) and Dalen Terry; Jaylin Williams out (back spasms). OKC lack wing size, so Cam Boozer could give them problems; Mara likely draws Edey/Boozer. Reporters expect a close OKC win at MEM with SGA closing (MEM's only closer is Jerome). Next: WAS on the 2nd night of a back-to-back (Caruso may rest), then POR twice in Portland. Hoop Collective (7 Nov): OKC lost three all-defensive players (Holmgren 8-10 weeks, Wallace, J. Williams); their defence was their offence (1st in points off turnovers each of the last 3 seasons) but they are about 22nd in the 6 games since. So SGA now works against set half-court defences loaded up on him; teams make Ajay Mitchell beat them. Discount OKC's season turnover/fast-break numbers in game_lens.
_team_notes.UTA: karma, 7 Nov: Utah are better than 1-7; their losing has been surprising. Measured: 7 of 8 games against MEM (x2), SAS (x2), POR, LAL, NOP; four of the seven losses by 9 or fewer (MEM 5, SAS 6, NOP 7, LAL 9); one win (NOP by 1). Their record is mostly schedule. Win the possession battle v DAL per game_lens (DAL -5.5/g, 27th).

Bam Adebayo.note: karma, watching MIA@GSW live (5 Nov US): Bam plays power forward next to Giannis, who takes the rebounds. Bam is pulled away from the rim to contest corner threes, so he is out of rebounding position. When Giannis sits, Portis comes in at centre (not Bam). In-game check: 1 reb in 11 min in Q1. So fade Bam's rebound overs when Giannis plays; Giannis's rebound overs look better. karma: he is still scoring (7 pts in Q1). The role moves his output from rebounds to points, so his points overs are fine and rebounds are the stat to fade. karma's rule: if we bet Bam, it has to be points + rebounds (PR), and only if the line is decent. No pure rebound props while he plays the 4 beside Giannis. karma (Q4, 5 Nov US): twice he was under the basket and made no effort for the rebound. He looks to be boxing out and leaving the board to Giannis, or is tired on the second night of a back-to-back after OT. Either way the rebound fade is real. Result 5 Nov: 18 pts, 10 reb in 33 min, so the rebound over still landed despite the low-effort stretches. MIA staggered him with Giannis (Giannis back in for Bam late Q1 and late Q2), so Bam gets solo-big minutes each half. Treat one game's effort read as a reason to prefer PR, not as a reason to bet the rebound under.
Bam Adebayo.review: check over the next 3-5 MIA games with Giannis playing

Bobby Portis Jr..note: Backup centre when Giannis sits (karma, live 5 Nov US).

De'Anthony Melton.note: karma (live, 5 Nov US): high-motor player, but too small to win rebounds against big frontcourts (MIA: Giannis, Bam, Portis). His RA leans on assists and steals-into-transition against big teams. The Dunker Spot: part of GSW's full-court pressure package, takes the ball off dribblers. Tentative: check against how the game ends (he had 2 reb, 2 ast in his first 5 min). karma: plays like a championship-core role player. Doesn't make mistakes and gives the team whatever it needs that night, which earns steady coach trust and minutes. His output moves between stats game to game, so bet him on combos (RA/PRA), not single stats.

Dylan Harper.note: Starting for SAS (karma, 6 Nov AEDT); our model has him at about 32 min. Treat him as a starter, not bench, in blowout and Cup-night reads. His PA o19.5 hit on 4 Nov.

Franz Wagner.note: Primary playmaker while Banchero (out since 24 Oct) and Suggs are out. Assists in those games: 9, 5, 11, 12, 6, then 15 vs PHX on 5 Nov (US), averaging about 10. Our model projected 5.6 because it leans on last season's role. Favour assist and PA overs while Banchero is out. karma flagged the 15-assist game live.

Draymond Green.note: karma (live, 5 Nov US): floor general and master small-ball centre who runs the offence from the 5. With Porzingis out he plays centre and the offence runs through him: 6 ast by halftime vs MIA, and 9 of his last 10 at 6+ ast before tonight. Our model's 24 min looks low when GSW's other bigs are out. Bet him on assists/RA, not points. Porzingis's absence is long-term (illness, no end point), so treat Draymond-at-centre as GSW's base setup this season. karma: Horford and Bassey are listed at centre and may start, but in big games (close games, closing lineups, Cup and playoff-type nights) it is still Draymond at the 5. Expect more Draymond minutes and assists on those nights.
Draymond Green.review: 2026-12-15 (Porzingis out long-term: karma 'out forever'; the Dunker Spot says no end point in sight)

Darius Acuff Jr..note: karma, 7 Nov AEDT (from watching him): when the Kings are losing by a big margin, Acuff checks out -- stands in the corner, his rebounds are accidental rather than chased. Avoid his overs (especially REB/PRA) when SAC is a big underdog / blowout risk.

Tyrese Maxey.note: karma, 7 Nov AEDT: if Maxey's first couple of shots don't fall and Brown, Edgecombe or Embiid are hot, he feels no pressure to keep shooting, so his volume drops. His PRA is points-heavy (few rebounds), so it rides on that. Be wary of his points/PRA overs when PHI is at full strength; better spots are when the other scorers sit.

LeBron James.note: Measured 7 Nov: 8+ reb & 8+ ast in 14 of 70 games in 2025-26; 11 of the 14 came with Luka and/or Reaves out (he became the main ball-handler), mostly in comfortable wins (+/- +7 avg), not tight games. 2 of 7 so far with PHI. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.note: karma, 7 Nov: he rises in big head-to-heads against other MVP candidates on national TV. Measured (game logs incl. playoffs): vs DEN/Jokic 2025-26 3-0 at 35.0 ppg (season 30.5); 2024-25 6-5 at 29.9 incl. the 7-game series OKC won. vs Luka's Lakers 2025-26 7-0 but only 25.9 ppg (wins, not points). Exception: vs SAS/Wemby 2025-26 4-7 at 27.2 ppg; his scoring dips against Wemby's rim protection. Lean his points over vs Jokic; be wary vs Wemby. Since J. Williams/Holmgren/Wallace went down, his shot volume jumped (35 and 26 FGA in his last two, 43 and 42 pts) and the ball is in his hands far more; our projection (31 pts) lags this usage spike, a role-change blind spot for a star. Beat reporters: his 19 FTA v CLE was inflated, about 10 were intentional fouls late; he is not top-10 in FTA this season, so don't bet his points on a free-throw story. Hoop Collective: '2015 Finals LeBron mode' - most shots of his career in a two-game span (36 misses), FG% down to the mid-40s from mid-50s; volume over efficiency while OKC are short. Points overs ride volume; efficiency-dependent props (FG made, 3PM) less so. karma, 7 Nov: never bet Shai unders (any stat, incl. quarter props like 1Q points). Check after OKC@MEM: his 1Q shots/points v a tout's 1Q under 9.5 (he was 9 and 9 in the two previous 1Qs). karma, 7 Nov: in the first couple of possessions he never looks to score; he gets teammates going first, then takes over. That explains his low 1Q scoring (about 5.8 avg). So: no 1Q points overs either; avoid Shai 'first basket' bets; his scoring is back-loaded (full-game points and 4Q are where he lives). MEASURED 7 Nov (ESPN PBP): 2026-27 by quarter avg 5.8 / 6.5 / 11.1 / 6.8 (1Q 9,0,5,2,4,8,9,9; Q3 is his biggest quarter, 37% of his points); first shot usually 1.5-4 min in. Last 12 games of 2025-26: 1Q 8.0 (28%), 10+ in 3 of 12. Read CONFIRMED: slow starter, third-quarter scorer.

Victor Wembanyama.note: karma, 7 Nov: he has openly said he wants the MVP this year (confirmed: preseason MVP favourite, said so publicly), so he will want to follow a big game with another. Isaiah Hartenstein.note: karma, 7 Nov: dominates the boards when he plays real minutes (14.7 reb/36). His 2026-27 duds are explained: the 3-reb opener at SAS was foul trouble with Chet and Aday Mara there to take his minutes, and the 7 at HOU was a blowout loss. Every other game since has been 12+. Rebound props hinge on minutes (~25 cap), not on matchup. karma: a master rebounder who reads angles and is very intentional, and always chases offensive boards because OKC isn't a good shooting team. Measured 2026-27: 27 of his 81 rebounds offensive (33%), 3.4 OREB a game in ~25 min.

Kyshawn George.note: karma, 7 Nov: really likes him, 'doing everything' vs ATL (attacking, rebounding, passing). 2026-27: 32.8 min, 17.2/4.2/4.8 (up from 14.8/5.1/4.5); 11 ast vs CLE, 25/4/7 last game vs ATL.
